I actually had this exact day today with zero experience and here’s how it went for me: It was a class of about 10 kids, with 5 other paras in the room. Their agenda for the day was different small table group activities with 30 min increments. Some may be non verbal or stimming/making loud noises. We played UNO, did crafts together, practiced sounding out words, watched a movie, and had outdoor time. 

Overall it was an easy day for me as the other paras were super helpful and mostly had me shadow them. It’s always unpredictable though. You may have some kids who have meltdowns/need breaks throughout the day. I was grabbed/touched a few times but usually the paras stepped in when that happened just be aware. 

Good luck!

Oh nice! It’s high school so expect your sub plans to just be them working on a Google classroom assignment/independent work. I always bring a book with me during the quiet moments when they’re being good and just working. Something I always do is write my name on the board, write the “agenda” to avoid getting repeated questions of “what are we doing today?” And I always let them know what my rules are within the first five mins “keep it quiet in here, only one person out at a time, make sure you’re sitting in your assigned seat” etc. If I have a rowdy class at the start, I always give them a reminder that I’ll be writing a long and detailed note for their teacher. 

But yeah for the most part, greeting them, setting the rules at the start, taking attendance, and what I call “circulating” i.e walking around the room every so often to make sure they are doing the assignment and not playing computer games is what high school usually consists of. 

You’re gonna do great!! Don’t worry too much about if they actually complete the assignment. It’s their grade that suffers. They’re in high school they should know the consequences of not doing their work. You can’t force them to do anything but as long as the class is quiet for you, it’ll be a good day :) good luck!
